Power 800: Evac+Chair Battery Powered Stair Climbing Chair
Product URL: https://www.anchortex.com/products/evac-chair-power-800-evacuation-stair-chair
Manufacturer page: https://www.evac-chair.com/evacuation-chairs/evacchair-power-800/
Spec sheet: Power 800 data sheet
Keywords (Ricky's sheet): Primary: stair climbing chair (250/mo, KD1). Secondary: battery powered stair chair (40), motorized stair climbing chair (20, KD1). Ricky's note: intent is mixed (daily care and emergency evacuation); check that the results page shows product pages, not stairlifts.
Recommended H1 and Subtitle
H1: Evac+Chair Battery Powered Stair Climbing Chair – Power 800
Current H1: Evac+Chair Power 1-800 Battery Powered Stair Chair for Daily Care and Emergency Evacuations
Subtitle: Motorized Stair Climbing Chair for Emergency Evacuation and Daily Patient Transport, Up and Down the Stairs with One Operator
Current subtitle: Evac+Chair 1-800 Battery Powered Stair Evacuation Chair
Revised Product Description
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
The Evac+Chair Power 800 is a battery powered stair climbing chair that carries a seated passenger up or down the stairs with no carrying or lifting. One operator guides the chair with a simple control panel, so staff can move a person with limited mobility between floors during a fire, power outage, or other emergency, and for daily patient transport.
A rechargeable lithium-ion battery charges fully in 1.5 hours, and a manual override lets the chair keep working without power. The motorized stair climbing chair folds for compact storage, opens in seconds, and is made with flame retardant, wipeable materials for hospitals, care homes, schools, offices, and high-rise buildings.
Operation: One person operation; motorized travel up and down the stairs, with no heavy lifting
Controls: Single speed control panel with on/off power and ascent and descent buttons
Battery: Rechargeable lithium-ion battery pack, fully charged in 1.5 hours, enough to go up and down a 5-story building 30 times
Manual Override: Switches the chair to manual operation when power is not available
Passenger Safety: Extra long quick release four point harness and a height adjustable padded headrest
Stair Track: Adjustable stair track with a tension control system (tool included)
Handles: Ergonomic adjustable operator handle, plus additional operator handles for added stability when a second operator helps
Wheels: Lockable rear wheels keep the chair stationary when needed
Visibility: LED safety light and photoluminescent branding for poor visibility
Frame: High strength aluminum frame
Infection Control: Wipeable materials, anti-microbial paint, and flame retardant materials
Folded Size: 19.5”W×10.6”D×45”H
Weight: 66 lbs
Certifications: FDA registered; CE and ISO 9001 certified
Compliance: Exceeds fire safety requirements and emergency response guidelines established to support the Americans with Disabilities Act
Includes: Rechargeable battery, battery charger, 2 keys, user guide, passenger headrest, passenger safety straps, photoluminescent wall sign, wall hooks, and dust cover
Warranty: Manufacturer’s warranty
Available Models and Options
Power 800 – Battery Powered Stair Climbing Chair: Up and down the stairs, one operator
[H2] Applications
The Power 800 suits buildings where people with limited mobility need to use the stairs, both in an emergency and day to day.
Typical applications include:
Emergency evacuation and power outages in multi-story buildings, when the elevators cannot be used
Daily patient transport between floors in hospitals, nursing homes, and care facilities
Schools, offices, hotels, and high-rise buildings
Homes, where a person needs help going up and down the stairs
Explore Anchortex's Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers collection for more evacuation equipment.
[H2] Frequently Asked Questions
Can the Power 800 go up the stairs?
Yes. The Power 800 is a battery powered stair chair that carries a passenger both up and down the stairs, with one operator.
How long does the battery last?
The lithium-ion battery charges fully in 1.5 hours, which is enough to go up and down a 5-story building 30 times.
What happens if the battery runs out?
The manual override switch turns the Power 800 into a manual stair chair, so it can still be used without power.
Can the Power 800 be used at home?
Yes. Evac+Chair recommends the Power 800 for home use, because it goes both up and down the stairs.
[H2] About Evac+Chair Evacuation Chairs
Evac+Chair makes stair evacuation chairs, powered stair chairs, evacuation sleds, and accessories for moving people with limited mobility on stairs, in an emergency or every day.
The Evac+Chair line includes:
Emergency evacuation chairs: The 300H, 400H, 600H, and 750H stair evacuation chairs for controlled travel down the stairs
Powered stair climbing chairs: The battery powered Power 800 and Power 900 for going up and down the stairs
Stair transport seat: The IBEX 700H Tran-Seat for two-person transport up and down the stairs
Evacuation sleds and mats: The Evac+Sled, Ulti-Mat, and Evac+Sheet rescue sheet
Accessories: Comfy Seat, transfer seat, storage cabinets, anti-theft alarms, and the iEvac smoke and fire escape hood
[H2] About Evac+Chair
Evac+Chair has made stairway evacuation chairs since 1982, and its chairs were designed in the United States. Explore the full line of Evac+Chair evacuation chairs at Anchortex.

Notes and Questions
Keywords: Ricky's primary keyword "stair climbing chair" is in the H1, the first sentence, the meta title, and the meta description. "Battery powered stair chair" and "motorized stair climbing chair" are in the subtitle, the intro, and the FAQs. The search results for "stair climbing chair" are product pages (electric stair chairs from Walmart, Vevor, Stryker), not stairlifts, so the term fits this product.
WEIGHT CAPACITY: our page and the Evac+Chair web page say 440 lbs, but the Power 800 data sheet and the Evac+Chair product range brochure both say 350 lbs. I left the capacity out until you confirm which is right.
Warranty: our page ends "Ask about their lifetime warranty," but the Evac+Chair brochure says the lifetime warranty excludes the Power 800, and the data sheet shows a one-year warranty seal. I wrote "Manufacturer's warranty." Should it say 1-year warranty?
Name: our product name says "Power 1-800" and the SKU is E601400. Evac+Chair calls it the Power 800, so I used Power 800. Is 1-800 the part number? If so, should it stay in the H1?
Shipping weight: the variant is set to 200 lbs. The chair weighs 66 lbs. Is 200 lbs the boxed weight? Should we change it?
Price: $3,225 with compare-at $4,300 (75%, not 80%). No change made.
Added from the Evac+Chair data sheet: "LED safety light and photoluminescent branding" (not on our current page).
Current meta description is a general GSA pricing line (109 characters). Is GSA pricing still offered? If so, should it go in the description?
Removed from the About section: "the original Emergency Evacuation Staircase Chair" and "the lifetime warranty" (see the warranty note).
FAQs: the 4 questions come from the Evac+Chair FAQ page and the data sheet. Competitor pages (Global Industrial, Walmart, Vevor) list capacity, steps per minute, and stairs per charge, but no FAQs.
Images: the page has only one image. Would you like me to add Power 800 photos from the Evac+Chair website?
